project_summary: Internal developer platform for a 200-person engineering org, built by a 4-person platform team to consolidate CI, CD, and observability.

failure_risks.risk: Adoption of the internal platform requires 200 engineers to migrate off existing tools; without a forcing function, voluntary migration will stall at low single-digit teams and the platform will be perceived as failed within 18 months.

action_map.validation_step: Determine whether voluntary adoption can reach critical mass.
action_map.minimum_test: Onboard 5 pilot teams over 8 weeks without executive mandate.

failure_risks.risk: The platform team of four cannot maintain breadth (CI, CD, and observability) plus build new features; the realistic delivery pace will fall below what staff engineers expect from internal tooling, eroding trust within the first year.

action_map.validation_step: Forecast team capacity against the planned scope.
action_map.minimum_test: Estimate maintenance burden for the existing toolchain and reserve 60% of team time for it.

failure_risks.risk: Cloud infrastructure costs for running the platform may exceed the savings from tool consolidation; without an explicit cost model, the platform may end up more expensive than the SaaS tools it replaces, killing executive support.

action_map.validation_step: Build a 12-month cost projection comparing platform spend vs. status quo.
action_map.minimum_test: Run the platform for 30 days at production scale and measure compute spend.
